quarterly_data.quarter: POSCO press release: [Special Interview] Dr. CHANG In Hwa, CEO of POSCO HOLDINGS (09-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CEO Chang In Hwa (company-published interview): POSCO operates oxygen plants at its Steel Works and POSCO Air Solution runs a separation and purification plant producing rare gases; through this process the group can cover approximately 50% of current domestic rare-gas demand. He said xenon, krypton, helium and neon are indispensable to the semiconductor industry, with xenon particularly crucial to the etching process for stacked devices such as HBM. The group is extending beyond lithium into rare earths and rare gases, building a value chain from resource acquisition through separation, purification and finished-product manufacturing.
quarterly_data.figure: rare-gas output can cover approximately 50% of current domestic rare-gas demand

quarterly_data.quarter: POSCO press release: [Special Interview] Dr. CHANG In Hwa, CEO of POSCO HOLDINGS (09-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CEO Chang In Hwa on portfolio direction (restating the July 2 CEO Investor Day): beyond supplying steel, POSCO group aims to supply materials for future industries such as AI and robotics and to widen its portfolio to Strategic Resources (represented by lithium) and Energy Resources. He cited a 20-year agreement securing LNG supply from Indonesia's Tangguh region (company says it was the first Korean company to sign with Tangguh LNG), the group's own LNG storage tanks and port facilities, and LNG transport, spot trading and midstream investment; he positioned LNG as the solution for power demand driven by the AI industry. He also said POSCO supplies automotive steel to Toyota, GM and Mercedes-Benz.
quarterly_data.figure: 20-year Tangguh LNG supply agreement; no financial figures stated
